title: MCP Tool block cannot execute on a Credential Group managed connection (mcp-cg-*)
body:
## Summary

The standalone **MCP Tool** block (`mcp`) cannot execute a tool on a Credential Group **managed connection** (`mcp-cg-*`). The identical tool, on the identical connection, executes successfully when reached through an agent's `mcp-server-advanced` tool.

## Reproduction

Workspace `6056c597-cd15-40a5-b6ba-831347b80473` (staging), one workflow, two runs minutes apart, same executing user (`theo@sim.ai`), same deployed workflow, after the Credential Group workflow-access grant was in place.

**Works** — agent block with `mcp-server-advanced`, `serverId: mcp-cg-GsSOF28euNUFuEWumbliB`
Run `449b4698-54f6-40b0-b1cc-3f64464f0622`. Trace shows spans executing successfully, e.g.

```
mcp-cg-GsSOF28euNUFuEWumbliB-fireflies_get_transcripts | success
```

**Fails** — `mcp` block, same connection
Run `e24ccdd6-97d6-4f59-ba55-d3d33cfa57ad`, and `205d0a1d-50ac-45f2-9330-8fe5008d05bd`.

```
input : {"tool": "fireflies_get_transcripts",
         "server": "mcp-cg-GsSOF28euNUFuEWumbliB",
         "arguments": {"fromDate": "2026-08-15", "mine": true, "limit": 25, "format": "json"}}
output: {"error": "Resource not found"}
```

Block inputs resolve correctly, and `createMcpToolId(server, tool)` yields `mcp-cg-GsSOF28euNUFuEWumbliB-fireflies_get_transcripts` — character for character the tool id that succeeds on the agent path.

## Ruled out

- **Tool id parsing.** `parseMcpToolTarget` handles the `mcp-cg-` prefix before falling through, and `parseMcpToolId` (which would mis-split `mcp-cg-<id>` into server `mcp-cg`) is only ever called from inside it.
- **The Credential Group policy.** Granting the workflow in `WorkflowCredentialAccess` fixed the agent path and changed nothing for the block. Both runs above are after the grant, deployed, so `execution:WorkflowMode` is `deployment`.
- **Connection ownership.** It fails using the executing user's *own* connection, not only another enrollee's.

## Not pinned

Remaining suspects are the block's dynamic tool resolution (`McpBlock.tools.config.tool` builds the id but `tools.access` is empty) and the `assertToolPermissionsWithRetry` preflight that runs for `mcp`-kinded tools, where the block and agent paths may present a different `resolveToolScope`.

## Why it matters

`mcp-server-advanced` exposes an entire MCP server to the model with no way to restrict it to read-only tools, and `usageControl: 'force'` governs *whether* a tool is called, not *which*. In an unattended ingest workflow this is a real hazard: with the agent workaround in place, a run whose query returned empty explored the surface and executed four mutations against a real Fireflies meeting — `move_meeting`, `update_meeting_privacy`, `create_soundbite`, `update_meeting_title`.

The `mcp` block is the correct shape for unattended work precisely because it calls exactly one named tool and cannot explore. While it does not work with managed connections, the safe shape is unavailable and the available shape is unsafe.

## Expected

`mcp` block with `server` set to an `mcp-cg-*` managed connection id executes the named tool, the same as `mcp-server-advanced` does.

title: Managed Slack enrollment: conversations.list returns the app's channel view while history calls act as the user
body:
## Summary

For a credential-group **managed Slack enrollment** (type `managed_oauth`, user token verified at enrollment with `token_type === 'user'` and the full `SLACK_MANAGED_USER_SCOPES` list including `groups:read`), tool calls diverge in identity **within a single workflow run**:

- `slack_v2` `get_channel_history` on a **human-to-human DM** of the enrollee succeeds — only the enrollee's user token can read that conversation.
- `slack_v2` `list_channels` in the same run, bound to the **same** `oauthCredential`, returns the **app's** channel view: only channels the Sim integration is present in, and omits private channels the enrollee is verifiably a member of.

## Reproduction (staging workspace 6056c597-cd15-40a5-b6ba-831347b80473)

Run `ingest-slack` (5a4c8be6-d148-4bd3-8596-dff2d464bd9e), deployed, async, input:
`{"subject":"marcus@sim.ai","credentialId":"ed101c5f-11c8-4580-9704-f2c2c00b4383","kbId":"…","dmChannelIds":"D0BAYR0HS3X"}`

Observed in run `518060e5-d667-46f0-9c34-6b9be5627fde` (2026-09-05):

- `listChannels` output: 17 conversations, all where the Sim app is present; `C0AMLFYRZU4` (#rvtech-internal, private) absent even though `conversations.members` confirms the enrollee `U0BB278QRRQ` is a member.
- `fetchHistory` on `D0BAYR0HS3X` (a DM between two humans, U0BB278QRRQ and U090GFBMY21): succeeds, 289+ messages written.

Reproduced for a second enrollee (theo@sim.ai, credential `6c86b682…`, run `0c9ca129…`): 20 conversations listed, #rvtech-internal absent despite membership. So it is systematic, not one credential.

## Why it matters

Any per-user Slack ingest driven by `conversations.list` silently sees only app-invited channels, so per-person corpora are built from the app's membership rather than the person's. Downstream this looks like missing data with no error anywhere.

## Notes for the fix

- The enrollment flow stores the `authed_user.access_token` (user token) — `apps/sim/lib/credential-groups/slack-managed-users.ts` enforces `token_type === 'user'`.
- `apps/sim/tools/slack/list_channels.ts` builds auth as `Bearer ${params.accessToken || params.botToken}`; both spans in the repro bind `oauthCredential`, so the substitution happens in server-side token resolution for the listing path, not in the block config.
- The custom bot service-account resolver (`SLACK_CUSTOM_BOT_PROVIDER_ID` in `apps/sim/lib/oauth/credential-service.ts`) returns the bot token; something appears to route `conversations.list` (and possibly other non-history reads) through it for managed enrollments.

title: Gmail Send / Draft: allow setting the From address (verified send-as alias)
body:
## Use case

One Google Workspace account (`ops@example.com`) with several verified **send-as aliases** (`billing@`, `sales@`, …). Different workflows should create drafts (and send) as different aliases, so the human who reviews a draft does not have to change the From address by hand before sending, and so the recipient sees the right address.

Gmail supports this natively: a message whose `From:` header is one of the account's verified send-as addresses (`users.settings.sendAs`) is accepted by `drafts.create` and `messages.send` and goes out from that alias. If the header is not a verified alias, Gmail silently rewrites it to the account's primary address, so this is safe by construction.

## Current behaviour

The Gmail tools have no way to set From. `buildSimpleEmailMessage` in `apps/sim/tools/gmail/utils.ts` assembles `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, `Subject`, threading headers and the body, and never emits a `From:` header, so every draft/send is attributed to the primary address. `GmailSendParams` (`apps/sim/tools/gmail/types.ts`) and the `draft_gmail` / `send_gmail` / `edit_draft_gmail` operations in `apps/sim/blocks/blocks/gmail.ts` expose no such field either.

## Proposal

Add an optional `from` parameter to the Gmail **Send**, **Draft** and **Edit Draft** operations:

- `GmailSendParams.from?: string`
- `buildSimpleEmailMessage`: when `from` is set, push `` `From: ${sanitizeHeaderValue(from)}` `` before `To:` (the attachment path that builds the MIME with attachments would need the same line).
- Block sub-block: a short text input "From (send-as alias)", optional, shown for the three operations, with a description saying it must be a verified send-as address on the connected account.

No scope change is needed: `gmail.compose` / `gmail.modify` already cover drafts and sends with a custom From. Optionally the block could offer a dropdown populated from `GET users/me/settings/sendAs`, but a free-text field is enough for a first version.

Happy to open a PR for this if useful.

title: UI: Make Skills a top-level sidebar resource, like Knowledge bases
body:
Finding and managing skills can be frustrating because they’re hidden as a tab within the **Integrations** section. Skills are content my team writes to shape how agents behave, so they're much closer to a Knowledge base than to an external service. Because of where they sit today:

- **Hard to find.** New builders don't expect Skills under Integrations, and many never learn the feature exists.
- **Wrong mental model.** Integrations are services you connect with credentials. Putting Skills next to them suggests a Skill is a kind of connector.
- **Confusing active state.** On `/skills`, the sidebar highlights **Integrations**, so it's unclear where you are.
- **Missing features other resources have.** Tables and Files get rail flyouts and appear in the `+` / `@` resource menus in Chat. Skills get neither.

Move Skills into the workspace resources section of the sidebar and give it the same UX as Knowledge bases.

- **Sidebar entry:** add a **Skills** nav item with its own icon, after Knowledge bases: `Tables · Files · Knowledge bases · Skills ·  Logs`. It's active on every `/skills/*` route, and Integrations is no longer highlighted there.
- **Rail flyout:** in the collapsed sidebar, hovering Skills shows recent skills and a **New skill** action, like Tables and Files.
- **Standalone page:** `/skills` gets the same layout as the Knowledge bases list: header, search, **New skill** / **Import**, and a resource list. Remove the Skills tab from the Integrations header.
- **Chat and search:** add Skills as a family in the `+` attach, `@` mention and resource-tab menus, in sidebar order. Open a skill as a resource tab in Chat, and make individual skills searchable in ⌘K.
- **Row actions:** give skill rows the same context menu as other resources: Open, Rename, Duplicate, Copy link, Manage members, then Delete after a separator.
- **Permissions:** add a `hideSkillsTab` permission-group option that works like `hideKnowledgeBaseTab`.
- **Backward compatibility:** keep existing `/skills` URLs and the legacy `?skillId=` redirect. Send any old Integrations → Skills links to `/skills`.

- **Keep Skills under Integrations and add a sidebar shortcut.** This helps people find Skills but keeps the wrong mental model and duplicates the entry point.
- **Put Skills inside Knowledge bases.** They're related, but Skills are instructions and Knowledge bases are searchable documents. Merging them would blur two different jobs.
- **Put Skills inside Agents.** Skills are shared across agents and workflows, so tying them to one agent's settings would hide their reuse.

- **Why it matters:** every resource an agent draws on (Tables, Files, Knowledge bases, Skills) should be found, opened and managed the same way. Skills are among the best ways to make agents reliable, so they should be easy to see.
- **Where it lives today:** the sidebar sets `additionalActivePaths: ['/workspace/{id}/skills']` on the Integrations nav item, the Skills page renders under `IntegrationTabsHeader`, and `RESOURCE_MENU_ORDER` has no skills family.

title: Feature request: recognise pay-per-call x402 results from MCP tools (pending payment response)
body:
Sim wires external MCP servers into canvas workflows and executes their tools. In `execute-tool.ts` (apps/sim/lib/internal/mcp/execute-tool.ts), a successful tool call returns `{ success: true, data: { success: true, output: result.output } }` — the MCP server's tool output is passed straight through to the workflow.

A **pay-per-call x402 MCP server** is a normal MCP server that answers a tool call with a pending-payment result instead of data: it returns HTTP 200 with result content of the form `{"status":"payment_required", "payment_challenge": {"price_xno": 0.0001, ...}}`. When a Sim workflow calls such a tool through `mcp-tool-selector`, `result.output` is that JSON blob, and the canvas shows raw JSON instead of a confirm-and-pay step. This has been verified against a live pay-per-call merchant MCP (Vend API Merchant at extract.paypercall.dev/mcp): `initialize` returns 200 with correct tools, but `tools/call` returns 200 whose result content is a `payment_required` envelope.

This is the one missing client-side behaviour for zero-signup pay-per-call tools to be usable from a Sim workflow — they already work at the MCP protocol level.

In the MCP tool-call path, detect a `payment_required` / x402 `payment_challenge` result structurally (not as raw JSON passthrough) and:

1. surface a per-call confirmable payment step — price, `pay_to`, scheme — so the operator can pay and retry from the canvas/UI, and/or
2. support an optional per-credential "payer" config so admin-added pay-per-call tools settle automatically under approval control.

Security invariant: no money moves unless the challenge parses AND the operator (or a configured, approved payer) approves.

- Keep raw JSON passthrough for paid tools. Works, but a workflow that dumps `payment_challenge` JSON to the user is not usable for pay-per-call tools.
- Build a separate x402 proxy outside Sim. Adds ops overhead and defeats the purpose of a visual MCP workflow.
- Use a custom extraction tool that pre-encodes the payment. Very platform-specific and doesn't leverage the growing x402 catalogue.

A working reference:
- **Vend API Merchant MCP manifest**: https://extract.paypercall.dev/.well-known/mcp
- **x402 settlement manifest**: https://extract.paypercall.dev/.well-known/x402
- 9 MCP tools (web extract, link check, geoip, web search, youtube transcript, etc.), single calls ~0.0001 XNO, no signup, no API keys, per-call settlement in Nano (XNO) via nano:mainnet.
- A bare probe returns 402 with the full challenge: `curl -i https://extract.paypercall.dev/api/v1/extract?url=https://example.com`

This is a first — Sim had zero x402 / pay-per-call coverage before this issue (GitHub search confirmed).
